verses.text: God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock with him in the ark. He sent a wind across the earth, and the floodwaters began to go down.
The springs of the deep and the sky's windows were shut, and the rain stopped.
The water kept draining from the earth. After 150 days, it had gone down.
The ark came to rest in the mountains of Ararat on the seventeenth day of the seventh month.
The water kept dropping until the tenth month. On the first day of that month, the mountain peaks appeared.
After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the water had dried from the earth.
He also sent out a dove to see if the water had gone down from the ground.
But the dove couldn't find anywhere to land, because water still covered the whole earth. It came back to Noah in the ark. He reached out, picked it up, and brought it inside.
Noah waited seven more days, then sent the dove out again.
The dove returned that evening with a freshly picked olive leaf in its beak. Noah knew the water had gone down.
He waited another seven days and sent the dove out again. This time it didn't come back.
On the first day of the first month of Noah's 601st year, the water had dried from the earth. Noah removed the ark's covering and saw that the ground was dry.
By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
Then God spoke to Noah:
"Leave the ark—you, your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives.
Bring out every living creature with you: the birds, the livestock, and everything that moves along the ground. Let them spread across the earth, have many young, and multiply there."
Noah went out with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.
Every animal, every creature that moves along the ground, and every bird left the ark, family by family.
Noah built an altar to Yahweh. He took one of every clean animal and clean bird and offered them as burnt offerings on the altar.

Yahweh smelled the pleasing aroma and said to himself, "I will never again curse the ground because of humans, even though their hearts lean toward evil from childhood. I will never again strike down every living thing the way I just did.
As long as the earth remains, planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will keep going."
